I can do MOK Enrollment without problems but Debian, Kali Linux, and Ubuntu show the following error: /EndEntire file path: /ACPI(a0341d0,0)/PCI(1,8)/PCI(3,0)/USB(5,0)/HD(5,11a2800,100000 /File(\EFI\boot)/File(shimx64.efi)/EndEntire Could not create MokListRT: Volume Full Could not create MokListXRT: Volume Full Could not create SbatLevel1RT: Volume Full Could not create MokListTrustedRT: Volume full Something is seriously wrong: import_mok_state() failed: Volume Full. The issues is in our Secure Boot design. You must change the design for multi-os to instead firmware -> one trusted shim -> GRUB signed by a key shim trusts -> signed kernels or firmware -> each distro's own shim+GRUB pair or firmware -> each distro's own shim+GRUB pair .
For Secure Boot:

BOOTX64.EFI should be shim.
mmx64.efi must be next to shim.
grubx64.efi must be signed.
Enroll one MOK certificate.
Sign your custom GRUB and any custom EFI binaries with that one key.
Do not enroll a new MOK per distro.
Do not keep testing with repeated MOK imports/deletes unless you clean pending variables afterward.

│     ├─ BOOTX64.EFI
│     ├─ shimx64.efi
│     ├─ mmx64.efi
│     ├─ grubx64.efi
│     └─ grub.cfg

You must incorporate to generate secure boot owned db.key, db.cer, db.esl, db.crt . These must be stored in secureboot folder on EFI partition on USB!! Except for db.key which is the private key and should be stored in /data/pki/secureboot/ . You must incorporate properly so that we own the whole secureboot chain and that user will manually import the db into the firmware secure boot chain so that it can be used instead of microsoft uefi etc.

  signs BOOTX64.EFI, GRUB, UKIs, EFI tools

  signs grub.cfg, kernels, initrds, manifests

Kernel module signing key:
  signs .ko modules

     Separate age threshold for non-idle huge-page recompress. Lets you protect recently-hot huge pages while still reclaiming older huge pages.
  16. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_INCOMPRESSIBLE_ONLY_IF_IDLE
     Controls whether incompressible pages must be idle before writeback, instead of the current cold or idle logic. This is a precise policy split for latency-sensitive systems.
  17. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_HUGE_RECOMPRESS_ONLY_IF_IDLE
     Controls whether type=huge recompress is allowed at all, or whether only huge_idle may be touched. This is more precise than a blanket “enable huge recompress” flag.
  18. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_FILL_PCT_FOR_RECOMPRESS_IDLE
     Separate fill threshold for idle recompress. Current code has one ZRAM_COLD_TIER_MIN_ZRAM_FILL_PCT gate for the whole cold-tier pass.
  19. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_FILL_PCT_FOR_RECOMPRESS_HUGE
     Separate fill threshold for huge recompress. Huge-page work may only make sense at higher zram occupancy.
  20. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_FILL_PCT_FOR_WRITEBACK_IDLE
     Separate fill threshold for idle writeback. Recompression and writeback are different costs; they should not share one occupancy gate.
  21. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_FILL_PCT_FOR_WRITEBACK_INCOMPRESSIBLE
     Separate fill threshold for incompressible writeback. Useful if you want incompressible spill only under tighter memory pressure.
  22. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_PRESSURE_SOME_FOR_RECOMPRESS
     Separate memory.pressure some avg10 gate for recompress work. Right now some/full thresholds gate the entire cold-tier run.
  23. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_PRESSURE_FULL_FOR_WRITEBACK
     Separate memory.pressure full avg10 gate for writeback work. This is a high-impact split because writeback is the backing-device-costly part.
  24. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_PRESSURE_FOR_INCOMPRESSIBLE_WRITEBACK
     Lets incompressible spill require actual pressure, while allowing less expensive recompression earlier.

Start should do:
1. acquire lifecycle lock
2. load zram module
3. open dm-crypt/plain ephemeral backing mapper
4. validate backing device is writable, unmounted, not active swap
5. clear stale signatures on backing mapper
6. reset /dev/zram0 if already initialized
7. configure compression algorithms
8. configure writeback backing device
9. configure writeback limits
10. set mem_limit
11. set disksize
12. mkswap
13. swapon
14. optionally emit a passive boot snapshot

Stop should do:
1. acquire lifecycle lock
2. swapoff /dev/zram0
3. reset zram device
4. close ephemeral backing mapper

Status print raw state but NOT allowed to make policy decisions:
initstate
comp_algorithm
recomp_algorithm
mm_stat
io_stat
bd_stat
debug_stat
swap status
backing device status

Reset should do:
1. acquire lifecycle lock
2. verify /sys/block/zram0 exists
3. if /dev/zram0 is active swap:
     swapoff /dev/zram0
4. wait until /dev/zram0 is no longer active in /proc/swaps
5. verify zram has no holders
6. if zram is already uninitialized:
     exit successfully
7. reset zram:
     preferred: zramctl --reset /dev/zram0
     fallback:  echo 1 > /sys/block/zram0/reset
8. wait until zram initstate/disksize confirms uninitialized

What wait-backing should do:
1. acquire lifecycle lock
2. validate backing config
3. ensure raw backing partition exists
4. load dm-crypt dependencies if needed
5. open ephemeral dm-crypt/plain mapper if not already open
6. if mapper already exists:
     verify it maps the expected raw backing partition
7. wait for /dev/mapper/<name> to appear
8. verify mapper is a block device
9. verify mapper is writable
10. verify mapper is not the same device as /dev/zram0
11. exit successfully

Wait backing should NOT do these:
do not reset zram
do not configure zram
do not set backing_dev
do not wipe signatures
do not mkswap
do not swapon
do not close mapper
do not run recompress/writeback policy

Conceptually, wait-backing: wait-backing = make sure encrypted backing block device exists and is usable

| Command        | Scope             |                   Destructive? | Touches dm-crypt mapper? | Touches zram? |
| -------------- | ----------------- | -----------------------------: | -----------------------: | ------------: |
| `reset`        | zram lifecycle    |           Yes, after `swapoff` |                       No |           Yes |
| `wait-backing` | backing readiness |                             No |      Opens/verifies only |            No |
| `start`        | full bring-up     | Yes, prepares backing and zram |                      Yes |           Yes |
| `stop`         | full teardown     |       Yes, disables swap/reset |            Closes mapper |           Yes |

 1. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_RECOMPRESS_IDLE_MAX_PAGES
     Independent page cap for the type=idle recompress path. Current code uses one shared ZRAM_RECOMP_MAX_PAGES for all recompress classes, which is too coarse for tuning idle versus huge work.
  2. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_RECOMPRESS_HUGE_IDLE_MAX_PAGES
     Independent page cap for type=huge_idle recompress. This is high-impact because huge-idle pages can dominate CPU cost on some hosts.
  3. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_RECOMPRESS_HUGE_MAX_PAGES
     Independent page cap for type=huge recompress. This is the most aggressive recompress path in the current design and should be bounded separately.
  4. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_WRITEBACK_IDLE_MAX_PAGES
     Hard cap for how many idle/cold pages one cold-tier pass is allowed to write back. The current code batches by generated page-index specs, but not by an explicit per-pass page ceiling.
  5. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_WRITEBACK_HUGE_IDLE_MAX_PAGES
     Separate cap for huge-idle writeback. Huge pages should not necessarily consume the same per-pass IO budget as ordinary idle pages.
  6. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_WRITEBACK_INCOMPRESSIBLE_MAX_PAGES
     Separate cap for incompressible-page writeback. This is one of the best knobs to add because incompressible pages are the clearest “spill first” class.
  7. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_RECOMPRESS_IDLE_MIN_PAGES
     Minimum candidate count before running idle recompress at all. Prevents paying recompress overhead for tiny candidate sets.
  8. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_RECOMPRESS_HUGE_IDLE_MIN_PAGES
     Minimum candidate count for huge-idle recompress. Useful because huge-idle passes are expensive and should not fire for a handful of pages.
  9. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_RECOMPRESS_HUGE_MIN_PAGES
     Minimum candidate count for huge recompress. This should be separate because huge is the most aggressive class currently touched.
  10. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_WRITEBACK_IDLE_MIN_PAGES
     Minimum idle/cold target size before issuing writeback. Reduces churn when the candidate set is trivial.
  11. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_WRITEBACK_HUGE_IDLE_MIN_PAGES
     Minimum huge-idle writeback candidate count. Keeps the huge-page writeback path from firing too often on marginal sets.
  12. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_WRITEBACK_INCOMPRESSIBLE_MIN_PAGES
     Minimum incompressible-page target size. This is especially useful on hosts where incompressible pages appear intermittently and you want fewer, more meaningful spill passes.
  13. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_HUGE_IDLE_MIN_AGE_SEC
     Separate age threshold for huge-idle handling. Current code uses the same ZRAM_IDLE_AGE_SEC and ZRAM_HOT_AGE_SEC logic for all classes. Huge pages usually deserve their own aging policy.
  14. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_INCOMPRESSIBLE_MIN_AGE_SEC
     Separate age threshold for incompressible-page writeback. Incompressible pages may be worth spilling sooner than ordinary idle pages.
  15. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_HUGE_MIN_AGE_SEC
     Separate age threshold for non-idle huge-page recompress. Lets you protect recently-hot huge pages while still reclaiming older huge pages.
  16. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_INCOMPRESSIBLE_ONLY_IF_IDLE
     Controls whether incompressible pages must be idle before writeback, instead of the current cold or idle logic. This is a precise policy split for latency-sensitive systems.
  17. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_HUGE_RECOMPRESS_ONLY_IF_IDLE
     Controls whether type=huge recompress is allowed at all, or whether only huge_idle may be touched. This is more precise than a blanket “enable huge recompress” flag.
  18. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_FILL_PCT_FOR_RECOMPRESS_IDLE
     Separate fill threshold for idle recompress. Current code has one ZRAM_COLD_TIER_MIN_ZRAM_FILL_PCT gate for the whole cold-tier pass.
  19. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_FILL_PCT_FOR_RECOMPRESS_HUGE
     Separate fill threshold for huge recompress. Huge-page work may only make sense at higher zram occupancy.
  20. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_FILL_PCT_FOR_WRITEBACK_IDLE
     Separate fill threshold for idle writeback. Recompression and writeback are different costs; they should not share one occupancy gate.
  21. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_FILL_PCT_FOR_WRITEBACK_INCOMPRESSIBLE
     Separate fill threshold for incompressible writeback. Useful if you want incompressible spill only under tighter memory pressure.
  22. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_PRESSURE_SOME_FOR_RECOMPRESS
     Separate memory.pressure some avg10 gate for recompress work. Right now some/full thresholds gate the entire cold-tier run.
  23. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_PRESSURE_FULL_FOR_WRITEBACK
     Separate memory.pressure full avg10 gate for writeback work. This is a high-impact split because writeback is the backing-device-costly part.
  24. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_REQUIRE_PRESSURE_FOR_INCOMPRESSIBLE_WRITEBACK
     Lets incompressible spill require actual pressure, while allowing less expensive recompression earlier.
  25. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_OPERATION_ORDER
     Explicit ordered list such as recompress_idle,recompress_huge_idle,recompress_huge,writeback_idle,writeback_huge_idle,writeback_incompressible,compact. Current sequencing is hardcoded. Making it
     configurable is valuable for experimentation without service sprawl.
  26. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_SKIP_WRITEBACK_IF_RECOMPRESS_SUCCEEDED
     Policy knob that says: if recompress reduced enough pressure, skip writeback this pass. This is a meaningful behavior lever and narrower than a generic enable flag.
  27. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_SKIP_COMPACT_UNLESS_WRITEBACK_OCCURRED
     Current code compacts when any operation succeeded. This knob would make compacting contingent on actual writeback activity, which is often the more useful case.
  28. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_SKIP_COMPACT_BELOW_FILL_PCT
     Compaction can be a cleanup optimization, not always worth the cost. This adds a precise condition instead of a global toggle.
  29. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_COMPACT_MIN_RECLAIMABLE_PAGES
     Only run compact if the candidate pass found enough reclaimable work. This is a better knob than simply “compact on/off”.
  30. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_WRITEBACK_SPEC_CHUNK_PAGE_LIMIT
     The current implementation chunks by spec string length and chunk count, not by explicit pages-per-spec. This would bound one sysfs writeback trigger more predictably.
  31. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_WRITEBACK_SPEC_CHUNK_COUNT_LIMIT
     Make the current internal MAX_WRITEBACK_CHUNKS_PER_CLASS effectively configurable instead of hardcoded. High-impact for bounding pass duration on very full systems.
  32. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_BLOCK_STATE_SCAN_LINE_LIMIT
     Make the block-state scan cap configurable instead of the hardcoded MAX_BLOCK_STATE_LINES. Useful for scaling the same logic between small and large memory hosts.
  33. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_CONSECUTIVE_NOOP_BACKOFF
     If N consecutive cold-tier passes produce no recompress/writeback/compact actions, stretch the next pass or short-circuit early. This is a high-impact runtime optimization.
  34. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_POST_ACTION_COOLDOWN_SEC
     Minimum wall-clock cooldown after a successful heavy pass. This is more precise than changing the systemd timer globally.
  35. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_FAIL_OPEN_ON_DEBUGFS_UNAVAILABLE
     Current logic falls back broadly when block-state is unavailable. This knob would let you choose strict versus permissive behavior when debugfs visibility is missing.
  36. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_EXPLICIT_PAGE_INDEX_MODE
     Control how ZRAM_MAINTENANCE_PAGE_INDEXES integrates with normal policy: prepend, append, only, or off. Current behavior is fixed and mixed into the pass.
  37. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_EXPLICIT_PAGE_INDEX_WRITEBACK_MAX_PAGES
     Separate per-pass cap just for explicit page-index injections. Useful for controlled experiments without letting operator-supplied specs dominate the whole pass.
  38. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_INCOMPRESSIBLE_PRIORITY
     Separate recompress/writeback priority ordering for incompressible pages relative to idle and huge pages. This is narrower and more expressive than a boolean flag.
  39. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_HUGE_PRIORITY
     Separate ordering bias for huge pages relative to idle pages. Helps when huge-page reclaim should happen earlier or later on specific storage classes.
  40. ZRAM_COLD_TIER_METRICS_DETAIL_LEVEL
     Controls how much state gets written into the metrics file per snapshot. This is valuable if snapshot cost itself becomes a concern, while still keeping behavior invariant.
